One day Abu Yazid washed his shirt outdoors. A companion said:
“Its owner has not given me permission.”
“The branches might break and be damaged.”
So Abu Yazid turned his back to the sun, laid the shirt across his own back and head, waited until it dried, and put it on again.
A Zoroastrian was told in Abu Yazid’s time:
If Islam is what Abu Yazid practises, I could never bear it.
And if Islam is what you practise, I have no desire for it.
The Sufis allowed a woman to receive the Sufi cloak of initiation from an unrelated man.
If her husband tried to prevent her, she could seek separation from him and go to her shaykh.
Ibn Aqil, one of the Hanbali theologians, said that much Sufi language points toward doing away with religious mediation and even prophecy itself.
When the Sufis spoke of hadith scholars, he said, they mocked them for having “taken their knowledge from one dead man after another.”
In this way, Ibn Aqil argued, they had already undermined prophecy.
My heart told me directly from my Lord
has openly declared that he has no need of the Messenger.
The heretics never dared openly reject religious law until the Sufis came along.
From the Words of the Sultan of Lovers
I pray, and sing of her. When I recite, it is her remembrance that fills me.
I sway with joy inside the prayer niche while she stands there before me.
On pilgrimage, when I enter consecration for the House, I enter in her name.
To abstain from her would be the breaking of my fast.
Whom could I follow in love if I ever sought escape from it?
Every imam in love follows me.
In every limb there is a longing for her, a yearning that pulls me by the reins.
Increase my bewilderment through the excess of love for You,
and let Your burning heat run through the veins of the earth.
And when I ask to see You as You truly are, then appear—
and do not answer me: “You shall not see.”
O heart, you promised me patience in loving them.
Take care, then, not to grow cramped or weary.
Tell those who came before me, and those who will come after,
and everyone who looks upon my grief:
take from me, follow my example,
listen to me, and speak of my affliction among the people.
I was alone with the Beloved. Between us was a secret
finer than the breeze when it begins to move.
I stood bewildered between His beauty and His majesty,
until the language of the state itself began to speak for me.
Be coy—you are made for it. Rule me: beauty has given you the right.
The command is yours. Judge my soul however you wish,
for beauty itself has appointed you over me.
Test me in your love however you please.
My only choice is whatever pleases you.
In every state you have a greater claim on me than I have on myself,
for without you I would never have been.
Beauty veiled in majesty leaves the lover lost,
Leave me my eyes. Perhaps one day before I die
I may see with them someone who has seen you.
How far I am from what I sought!
And how could my eye receive its share when it has never seen you?
Everyone touched by beauty loves you, but I alone love everyone within your sanctuary.
The lovers will be gathered beneath my banner,
and every beautiful one beneath yours.
Your distance from me is itself a kind of nearness,
and inside your coldness I have found tenderness.
Whenever you disappear outwardly from my sight,
I turn inward in a thousand directions and find you a thousand times.
It is no wonder that light is borrowed from my outward form,
when my inward being is your home.
From the Great Ode Rhyming in Tāʾ
Speak of beauty as absolute. Do not confine it
by tying it to ornament and decoration.
The beauty of every beautiful man is borrowed from hers,
and so is the beauty of every beautiful woman.
Through her, Qays fell mad for Lubna. Through her, every lover has fallen—
Majnun for Layla, Kuthayyir for Azza.
Every one of them longed for an attribute she had put on,
a beauty appearing inside a beautiful form.
It was only she appearing through different manifestations.
They imagined someone else, although it was she who appeared within them.
She appeared by hiding and hid by appearing,
taking on one form after another in every manifestation.
At the beginning of creation she appeared to Adam
in the form of Eve, before Eve became a mother.
He fell in love with her so that through her he might become a father,
and through the pair the law of children might appear.
She has never stopped appearing and disappearing,
according to the needs of every time and every age.
